terms.title: Attribute Anomaly
terms.summary: The attribute-linked effect inflicted when an enemy's Anomaly Buildup reaches its limit.
steps: Attacks and skills that inflict Anomaly Buildup fill the enemy's gauge for that Attribute.
When the gauge reaches its limit, the corresponding Attribute Anomaly is inflicted.
The result depends on the Attribute and on the Agents that contributed to the buildup.
terms.whyItMatters: Attribute Anomaly connects application speed, the resulting effect, reaction timing, and damage. Reading those as separate layers makes team and rotation advice much easier to evaluate.
terms.distinction: Anomaly Buildup fills the gauge. Attribute Anomaly is the effect inflicted when that gauge reaches its limit. Anomaly is also an Agent specialty, so the same word can refer to a role rather than the combat effect.

statNotes.name: Anomaly Mastery (AM)
statNotes.description: Scales how quickly an Agent applies Anomaly Buildup. At the base-stat level, more AM means more buildup from the same move.

statNotes.name: Anomaly Proficiency (AP)
statNotes.description: Scales Attribute Anomaly damage. It does not make the buildup gauge fill faster.

gauge.label: Anomaly Buildup
gauge.caption: Separate Attributes build separate gauges. The ring is a schematic of the in-game buildup indicator, not a screenshot.

applicationRules.name: ICD — internal cooldown
applicationRules.description: A normal Attribute Anomaly cannot be retriggered immediately. Controlled v1.1 testing measured a roughly three-second lock for the same anomaly; a current v3.1 regression test is still needed.

applicationRules.name: A full gauge may wait
applicationRules.description: In the v1.1 test, the capped gauge did not trigger automatically when the lock expired; a subsequent eligible buildup hit triggered it. Excess buildup while capped could be lost.

applicationRules.name: Resistance changes buildup
applicationRules.description: Enemy Anomaly Buildup RES changes how much effective buildup a move contributes. Exact stacking, caps, and negative-RES behavior belong in a tested formula note.

applicationRules.name: Not generic stat diminishing returns
applicationRules.description: AM and AP scale their base roles linearly. Practical saturation comes from ICD, resistance, and contributor mix—not an intrinsic AM or AP penalty. Older mechanics references reported repeated-trigger threshold growth, but its current v3.1 behavior and reset condition are unverified.

effects.description: Assault deals Physical damage and interrupts. Flinch increases the Daze the target takes for a period.
Burn deals Fire damage over time. Application can interrupt enemies weak to Fire.
Freeze stops action; ending it causes Shatter damage. Frostbite increases CRIT DMG taken for a period.
Attacks against a Shocked target can cause additional Electric damage during the effect.
Attacks against a Corrupted target can cause additional Ether damage during the effect.
Windswept follows its own interaction path: eligible follow-up damage establishes Contamination, and Vortex replaces the usual Disorder route.

interactions.name: Disorder
interactions.description: A different eligible anomaly replaces the active one, dealing additional damage and accumulating Daze. Normal Disorder historically produced a wider ICD lock.

interactions.name: Vortex
interactions.description: Windswept plus another anomaly triggers Vortex instead of normal Disorder. Its exact coefficients and retrigger timing remain open.

interactions.name: Abloom
interactions.description: Certain Agent skills use an existing Attribute Anomaly to deal additional Attribute Anomaly damage. The triggering skill defines the calculation.

interactions.name: Polarized Assault
interactions.description: Alice's named Assault mechanic can ignore normal buildup progress. It is not a generic category called “Polarize.”

interactions.name: Polarity Disorder
interactions.description: A distinct special trigger that deals extra damage without removing the active Attribute Anomaly.

interactions.name: Lumiflux · Refringe
interactions.description: Lumiflux uses its own buildup and reaction rules. It should not be described as simply filling a normal gauge to inflict a Lumiflux Anomaly.

formulaNotes.name: Buildup map
formulaNotes.formula: Base Buildup × (AM ÷ 100) × buildup bonuses × target RES modifier
formulaNotes.status: Historical mechanics model — needs v3.1 regression

formulaNotes.name: Damage map
formulaNotes.formula: Base Anomaly DMG × (AP × 0.01) × level and combat modifiers
formulaNotes.status: Baseline model — special mechanics can replace it

formulaNotes.name: Contributor model
formulaNotes.formula: The result reflects the Agents that contributed buildup and their respective shares.
formulaNotes.status: Current wording, open calculation — needs instrumentation

terms.freshnessNote: Core lifecycle and named mechanics were checked for version 3.1. Exact ICD timing and formulas are labeled where the best reproducible evidence is historical or still needs live instrumentation.

terms.title: Disorder
terms.summary: The reaction caused when a different eligible Attribute Anomaly replaces one already active on an enemy.
steps: Inflict an Attribute Anomaly on an enemy.
Inflict a different eligible Attribute Anomaly while the first is active.
The first anomaly is replaced and Disorder deals additional damage and accumulates Daze.
terms.whyItMatters: Disorder rewards teams that coordinate more than one Attribute, but its damage depends on the anomaly being removed and how much of its effect remained.
terms.distinctionTitle: Not every anomaly interaction is Disorder
terms.distinction: Wind uses Vortex when Windswept is involved. Polarity Disorder is a separate special mechanic and does not remove the active anomaly.

statNotes.name: Removed anomaly
statNotes.description: The outgoing anomaly determines the base Disorder behavior.

statNotes.name: Time remaining
statNotes.description: Standard damage-over-time anomalies generally produce more Disorder damage when replaced earlier. Extended-duration and special anomalies need separate testing.

related.name: Attribute Anomaly
related.description: The buildup, trigger, and effect system that Disorder reacts to.

related.name: Polarity Disorder
related.description: A special trigger that does not remove the active anomaly.

terms.title: Abloom
terms.summary: A named mechanic used by certain Agent skills to deal additional damage from an existing Attribute Anomaly.
steps: An Attribute Anomaly is active on the target.
An Agent skill with an Abloom trigger meets its conditions.
Abloom deals additional Attribute Anomaly damage using that skill's own calculation.
terms.whyItMatters: Abloom is a real shared label, but not a universal reaction with one fixed multiplier. Its trigger and scaling must be read from the Agent skill that produces it.
terms.distinctionTitle: A category, not a free reaction
terms.distinction: An ordinary Attribute Anomaly does not automatically cause Abloom. A compatible Agent skill has to trigger it, and different implementations can use different ratios.

statNotes.name: Existing anomaly
statNotes.description: Abloom derives damage from an Attribute Anomaly already present on the target.

statNotes.name: Skill-defined scaling
statNotes.description: The triggering Agent's skill defines the exact damage calculation.

related.name: Attribute Anomaly
related.description: The base system from which Abloom derives its damage.

terms.freshnessNote: Official material supports Abloom as a named damage mechanic. Treat every exact ratio as kit-specific and version-sensitive.

terms.title: Polarized Assault
terms.summary: Alice's named Assault mechanic, which can deal Assault damage without following the normal buildup trigger.
steps: Alice meets the skill-specific conditions for Polarized Assault.
The effect ignores normal Anomaly Buildup progress.
It deals damage equivalent to regular Assault and can participate in Disorder interactions.
terms.whyItMatters: Polarized Assault is an exception to the normal fill-the-gauge trigger flow and should not be generalized to other Agents or treated as a system-wide “Polarize” category.
terms.distinction: Polarized Assault is Alice's mechanic. Polarity Disorder is a different special mechanic associated with other Agents and does not remove the active anomaly.

statNotes.name: No normal buildup trigger
statNotes.description: The skill can produce its Assault-equivalent effect without filling the Physical buildup gauge in the ordinary way.

statNotes.name: Agent-specific rule
statNotes.description: Its activation and scaling belong to Alice's kit, not the base Attribute Anomaly rules.

related.name: Attribute Anomaly
related.description: The normal gauge-and-trigger flow that Polarized Assault bypasses.

related.name: Polarity Disorder
related.description: A separate special mechanic with a similar-looking name.

terms.freshnessNote: The official release spelling is Polarized Assault. Do not preserve “Polarity Assault” as an alias without reproducing it in the current English client.

terms.title: Polarity Disorder
terms.summary: A special Disorder-like trigger that deals extra damage without removing the active Attribute Anomaly.
steps: An eligible Attribute Anomaly is active on the enemy.
A compatible Agent skill triggers Polarity Disorder.
It deals additional damage while leaving the active anomaly in place.
terms.whyItMatters: Because it does not replace the active anomaly, Polarity Disorder does not follow the same state transition as normal Disorder and must be modeled separately.
terms.distinctionTitle: It does not consume the active anomaly
terms.distinction: Normal Disorder replaces the first anomaly when another eligible one is inflicted. Polarity Disorder is skill-triggered and leaves the active anomaly in place.

statNotes.name: Active anomaly retained
statNotes.description: The target keeps the Attribute Anomaly that enabled the trigger.

statNotes.name: Kit-defined damage
statNotes.description: The compatible Agent's skill defines the exact scaling and conditions.

related.name: Disorder
related.description: The normal reaction whose name this special mechanic modifies.

related.name: Polarized Assault
related.description: Alice's separate mechanic with a similar-looking name.

terms.freshnessNote: Polarity Disorder is a skill-defined special mechanic. Agent availability, triggers, and ratios can change with kit and version updates.
